title: Cap. 3 Obj. 11: Death not applicable to those for whom Christ was not offered — the non-elect
pass_a_gloss: Obj.11: death not applicable to those not died-for; countless non-elect. Minor from Rom 8:32 — God gives all to those Son died for; not all get all so not died for all. Sol: grant where God in no way willed death. Lytron sufficient even for fallen angels, but defect of ordination/acceptance = not for angels. No sharer of assumed nature without applicable redemption-price for remission through faith. Rom 8 not to any humans but elect already called/justified/sanctified (Col 1:13). Not all-things to all-died-for but to present discourse = predestined believers already specially given Christ. Stretch beyond predestination/calling/justification exceeds Apostle.
pass_b_english: Obj. 11. Christ's death is not applicable to those for whom he did not die or was not offered: But there are countless human beings for whom he did not die or was not offered, namely all those who were not enrolled in the register of the elect before the foundations of the world were laid. From this they try to confirm the Minor, because the Apostle expressly asserts that God wills to grant all things to those for whom the Son died, ([[Romans 8:32 >> Bible:Romans 8:32]]): He who did not spare his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, how will he not also with him freely give us all things? But he does not freely give all things to all: Therefore Christ did not die for all: Therefore his death is not applicable to all.

Sol. I gladly grant that Christ's death can in no true sense be said applicable to those for whom God in no way willed him to die. For Christ's death is not a remedy applicable to expiating anyone's sins except by God's ordination and acceptance. And for this reason, although the lytron paid by Christ to God the Father is in itself of sufficient and superabundant value for redeeming the sins not only of human beings but of fallen angels, yet because of the defect of ordination and acceptance as to the angels, we truly deny that Christ ought to be said to have died for them in any way. The same would have to be held of those human beings too, if there were any who by the same defect of Divine ordination and acceptance were alien and excluded from every possibility of the said redemption. But as has been said, the Major being granted, let us come to the Minor. I answer therefore, That there is no one sharing the same human nature which the Redeemer deigned to assume, for whom Christ has not delivered himself as a redemption-price applicable by God's ordination and acceptance for obtaining remission of sins through faith in his blood. Nor does the Apostle contradict us, whose whole discourse in Romans 8 does not look to consoling any human beings whatever placed in any state, but the elect; nor the elect simply, but the elect already called, justified, sanctified, that is, as the same speaks in ([[Colossians 1:13 >> Bible:Colossians 1:13]]), already delivered from the power of darkness, and transferred into the kingdom of the Son of his love. Nor does he affirm simply and universally that God freely gives all things to all human beings for whom Christ died, but to all those of whom the present discourse is instituted, that is, to all the predestined believing in Christ, for whom not only did Christ die, but to whom moreover Christ has already been given in a special mode, that is, united, and communicated with the infinite treasure of his merits. This consolatory argument of the Apostle drawn from Christ's death is therefore efficacious, but if it is accommodated to those and so far, to whom and so far as it was accommodated by the Apostle: namely in this way, You who from your effectual calling, justification and sanctification can already acknowledge and feel that you are predestined, and that God in specially and effectually redeeming you willed his Son not only offered to himself, but also communicated to you, how can you not trust that he will for the rest freely give you all other things necessary for consummating salvation? But if anyone should wish to apply the aforesaid reason to any human beings whatever, setting aside consideration of predestination, calling, justification, in this way, Christ died for you, or Christ gave himself a lytron or victim to God for expiating your sins, therefore God will also freely give you all things, I say he draws this argument beyond its limits contrary to the Apostle's mind; who narrowed it to certain persons, namely the predestined, and those already placed in a certain state, namely of justification and adoption.
